Genuine internal timeout reaches that same close seam; exit fails closed if restoration was not confirmed, never fabricates Stop. Default nonC6 branch unchanged.

Diagnostic and original stderr bytes are privately scanned before parse or content checks; record count, identity, markers, bounds and presence assert fixed scalar values only. Diagnostic parse failure uses a fixed closed assertion without raw parser cause. No message/stderr/runtime ID/list contents are AssertJ actual/expected values.

One selected C6 restoration closure remains reachable via original runtime tag and existing producer seal command. Both fulfilled and rejected original stop results call it, with original result untouched. Busy deadline or failed descriptor restore remains sticky and retains closure/tag for bounded later retry. Only actual busy=false and exact restore remove the tag/capability. Failed original close remains a distinct sticky failure and cannot emit a successful-close receipt. Outer finally attempts the seal retry and quarantines unresolved restoration/drain while retaining the C5 comparator/capture for late failures.

Every RuntimeException validation/response failure remains sticky, including secondary query/identity validation. Only an accepted selected focus-enter response IOException can be held as provisional transport unavailability. No cut timestamp exemption remains. Terminal classification requires actual original Node pending, actual original context close, unavailable page fence and exact unknown closed-phase receipt; otherwise fails. No healthy page ACK or no-effect credit.

Each existing case now requires exactly one actual terminal USAGE, code UNKNOWN_OUTCOME, and one actual DISPATCH RESOLVED RELEASE. It requires exact release-id/partition linkage, no affected-release surrogate, version/sequence/scope/principal/test/source/coordinate equality through existing p4CompareAuditScope, and authentic consumed guided admission/materialization or ordinary accepted attempt/admission/revision binding through p4AuditOwnerIdentity.
